statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH (yellow). The 29,231.00 session low set in the previous hour has held for roughly an hour with no new extension, NQ trades 29,262.50 down 187.00 points or 0.63%, and ES holds above its own 7,645.25 low. VIX has eased from its 18.03 session high to 17.88 while the 10-year at 5.03%, the 2-year at 4.68% and WTI at 103.65 are unchanged on the hour, so Tail eases from 25 to 24 and Stress from 76 to 75.
recommendation: Tail at 24 maps to WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD, one point below the block threshold that the previous hour crossed. The change records a specific stabilisation rather than a general improvement in tone. The break of the 29,308.50 shelf produced one clean extension to 29,231.00 and then stopped: that low has now survived roughly an hour of testing, ES has not made a new low beneath 7,645.25 either, and two independent quote sources put NQ at 29,262.50 and 29,266.75 within the same minute. The framework treats repeated extension after failed retracements as the qualifying Tail structure, and the second extension has not arrived. The cross-asset amplifiers that aligned an hour ago have also stopped intensifying. The US 10-year is unchanged at 5.03%, still its highest since 2007, the 2-year at 4.68% and the 30-year at 5.40% leave the curve steepening from the long end, and WTI at 103.65 is within a penny-scale distance of where it traded an hour ago inside a 101.83 to 103.96 range. Cash VIX has come off its session high rather than pressing it, which is the volatility decay the framework treats as a reason to let Tail fall. What keeps the score at 24 rather than lower is that none of this is repair: NQ sits about 31 points above its session low, the broken shelf overhead is unrecovered, the Saudi East-West pipeline is still shut with briefed officials citing three to five weeks of repair work, and the Federal Reserve decision on 16 September arrives with reporting putting futures-implied odds of a rate increase above 90%. The declared danger window is unchanged at 13:00 to 15:00 UTC around the US cash open, which remains the first deeply liquid test of a structure that is broken rather than merely tested. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected by the mapped state.
headline: NQ holds the 29,231.00 low for an hour without extending and VIX eases off its high - Tail steps back to 24 and the mapped state returns to WATCH
body:
The development of this hour is an absence: the extension that would have confirmed last hour's break did not arrive. NQ set 29,231.00 in the previous window and that low has now held for roughly an hour. The contract trades 29,262.50, down 187.00 points or 0.63% against a 29,449.50 prior close, with the session range unchanged at 29,231.00 to 29,495.25. A second independent quote source puts the same contract at 29,266.75, down 0.62%, against the identical 29,231.00 low, so the price path this hour is corroborated rather than single-sourced.

ES tells the same story. It trades 7,650.25, down 0.55%, and its 7,645.25 low is also unchanged from the previous hour. An hour ago the notable feature was that ES had begun confirming NQ's break; this hour neither index future has made a new low. The framework's qualifying Tail structure is repeated extension after failed retracements, and the sequence has so far produced one extension and then a stall.

The cross-asset alignment that formed an hour ago is intact but no longer intensifying, and one leg has started to decay. The US 10-year Treasury yield is unchanged at 5.03%, up about 4.6 basis points on the day and still the highest since 2007, with the 2-year at 4.68% up under a basis point, the 5-year at 4.86% and the 30-year at 5.40%. That is the same bear-steepening configuration as an hour ago, not a further leg. WTI trades at 103.65, up 2.23%, inside an unchanged 101.83 to 103.96 range. Cash VIX is the one that has turned: at 17.88 it is up 4.56% on the day but below the 18.03 session high it was pressing an hour ago. Volatility fading off its extreme while price holds above its own extreme is the combination the framework treats as grounds for Tail to ease rather than build.

The energy story remains unresolved but has acquired a second side. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline is still shut after drone strikes traced to Iraqi territory, and regional officials briefed on the damage have told the Associated Press that repairs to a major pumping facility could take three to five weeks, while adding that the line could operate partially during that work. Against that, the US Energy Secretary said on Monday that the line should be back online soon. The 1,200-kilometre pipeline carries up to seven million barrels a day and exists specifically to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, so the outage is a genuine supply discontinuity rather than a scheduled catalyst. A story with a credible restoration path, however, is a weaker one-way amplifier than a story that only deteriorates.

The equity-specific driver is unchanged from Monday and remains rotational rather than uniform. The selloff followed industry calls to slow frontier AI model development and hit semiconductors hardest, with the chip complex down sharply across every tracked name, while Communication Services closed higher and megacaps finished split. Reporting characterises the move as sentiment-driven, noting that no hyperscaler cut capital-expenditure guidance. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Monday at 29,127.16, down 0.82%, but only after dipping to 28,867.67 and recovering more than 259 points into the close, which is itself a mean-reversion outcome.

The shared Finviz cross-asset context file was not usable this hour. It was collected at 06:47 UTC, roughly two and a half hours before this assessment, and carries a partial collection status with its calendar section unavailable. Under the applicable contract that context is treated as stale and the assessment rests entirely on independently verified primary sources. Because the file only ever supplies delayed, latest-session context rather than live price-path evidence, its absence does not degrade the live evidence this hour and Confidence stays at 87.

Three scheduled US items fall in today's session: weekly ADP employment at 12:15 UTC, the NY Empire State manufacturing index at 12:30 UTC and a 20-year bond auction at 17:00 UTC. None had printed at the assessment cutoff and none is treated as an automatic block. The two-day Federal Reserve meeting that opened on 15 September concludes with the decision and projections at 18:00 UTC on 16 September and a press conference at 18:30 UTC, both beyond this forecast horizon. Current reporting puts futures-implied odds of a policy-rate increase above 90%, an unusual configuration against a long end already at multi-decade highs.

The dominant mode returns to mixed. The one-way character that justified trend-down an hour ago has dissipated into a roughly 60-point consolidation above the low, with the broken shelf unrecovered overhead and no recovery attempt of consequence either. The forecast holds 24 through the European mid-morning window that produced Monday's chip-led leg, eases to 23 into the pre-US lull, returns to 24 for the 12:15 and 12:30 UTC releases, and peaks at 27 across the declared 13:00 to 15:00 UTC danger window covering the cash open and the first full cash hour. That peak is held in the lower half of the elevated band because no opening structure has been observed and Monday's equivalent session recovered. Conditional risk then decays through the US afternoon, with a 25 tick for the 20-year auction, and falls to a cycle low of 17 in the Asian session before rebuilding into the European open on Federal Reserve decision day.

lookbackSummary: The published record covers all 24 preceding clock hours with no gaps. Tail ran 20 to 26 through Monday's European and US morning, peaking at 26 twice around the chip-led decline and the US cash open, then decayed through the US afternoon to 15 and to a 14 trough in the Asian session as price discovery turned orderly. It re-accelerated to 24 at 05:00 UTC when NQ first broke the 29,426.75 shelf with both index futures at extremes, eased to 20 and 21 through the European pre-open as a retracement resolved that structure, and reached 25 at 08:00 UTC when the subsequent floor also failed. Stress held a 65 to 79 band throughout, reflecting a rate and energy backdrop that never reset. Confidence stayed between 86 and 89 on continuously available price-path evidence.
outlookSummary: The conditional path holds 24 for the remainder of this hour and across the 10:00 UTC window that produced Monday's chip-led leg, which now opens with the overnight floor broken but holding. It eases to 23 for the pre-US lull, returns to 24 for the 12:15 and 12:30 UTC releases, and peaks at 27 across the declared 13:00 to 15:00 UTC danger window covering the US cash open and the first full cash hour. That peak stays in the lower half of the elevated band because no opening structure has been observed and Monday's cash session recovered more than 259 points from its low. It steps down to 24 and 23 through the US afternoon, ticks back to 25 for the 17:00 UTC 20-year bond auction given the long-end repricing, and holds 23 into the closing hour. After the 20:00 UTC cash close conditional risk decays through 21, 20, 19 and 18 into the Asian session, bottoming at 17, before rebuilding through 18, 19, 20, 21, 22 and 23 into the European morning on Federal Reserve decision day. Stress tracks the same shape between 78 and 66 without leaving the high band, because a 5.03% 10-year and an unrepaired Saudi pipeline do not reset overnight.
